definitions.explanation: Attached to a place name to name the way people speak there, as in Kansai-ben or Hiroshima-ben. This is the use most learners meet.
Skill with words, or what someone says on an occasion; used in a few set phrases and in news writing.
A device that opens and closes to control the flow of a liquid or gas, and the valves of the heart.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{関西|かんさい}{弁|べん}→関西弁：17855_kansaiben⟧, ⟦{東北|とうほく}→東北：27542_touhoku⟧{弁|べん}, ⟦{博多|はかた}→博多：31872_hakata⟧{弁|べん}: Kansai, Tohoku, Hakata dialect
- ⟦{弁|べん}が{立|た}つ→弁が立つ：20076_bengatatsu⟧: to be eloquent, to have a way with words
- 〜⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{弁|べん}: someone's remarks (⟦{就任|しゅうにん}→就任：12368_shuunin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{弁|べん}, remarks on taking office)
- ⟦{安全|あんぜん}→安全：01131_anzen⟧{弁|べん}: safety valve, also figurative

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{方言|ほうげん}→方言：07419_hougen⟧: dialect; the general and academic word. 〜{弁|べん} names a particular one and is the everyday way to say it.
- ⟦{標準語|ひょうじゅんご}→標準語：07421_hyoujungo⟧: standard Japanese, the opposite of 〜{弁|べん}

WATCH OUT:
⟦{便|べん}→便：26147_ben⟧ (stool, bowel movement) has the same reading; in context the two are never confused.
